observations:
Torah #195 is one of the shortest Torahs in Likutay Moharan Vol. 1 — 3 lines interpreting a single verse (Psalms 4:2). The teaching contains only one conceptual domain: the paradox of הרחבה (expansion) found within the צרה (distress) itself, perceived through the lens of חסדי ה' (God's kindnesses).

The three bechina-eligible concepts identified in the source text (צרה, הרחבה, חסדי ה') form a single unified cluster — the 'Expansion Within Distress' package proposed in torah_195_additions.json. This is not a new package in the sense of a domain independent of existing additions; it IS the primary package for Torah #195, constructed from scratch since the dataset contains zero bechina edges for this Torah.

Candidate domains examined and rejected for independent new-package status:

1. SALVATION / RESCUE DOMAIN: The text briefly mentions the hope for future salvation — 'מִלְּבַד מַה שֶּׁאָנוּ מְצַפִּים שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ בְּקָרוֹב מִכָּל הַצָּרוֹת' (besides what we await — that God will save us soon from all troubles). This is a parenthetical contrast, not a developed domain. The text immediately returns to the main point. Only one concept (ישועה/salvation) could be extracted, which is insufficient (need 3+) for a new package.

2. PRAYER / CONTEMPLATION DOMAIN: The act of הסתכלות (looking/contemplating God's kindnesses) is the practical element of the teaching. However, this is eitza language — it describes what a person DOES to perceive the hidden expansion, not what something essentially IS. No bechina-type cluster around prayer or contemplation can be extracted from a 3-line text that does not mention תפלה, עבודה, or related prayer concepts.

3. GOOD/EVIL MIRROR: Rebbe Nachman's teachings typically have an evil mirror for each good cluster. Torah #195 is unusual in that it contains no evil counterpart concepts whatsoever. The teaching is purely about divine goodness operating within apparent difficulty — there is no antagonist force, no sitra achra, no evil dimension named in the text. This is consistent with the teaching being an extremely short, focused theological affirmation (essentially a one-line commentary on a Psalm verse), not a full structural teaching with opposing forces.

SUMMARY: Torah #195's entire bechina content collapses into one cluster: the paradoxical unity of צרה and הרחבה within חסדי ה'. This constitutes the foundational package (proposed in additions file) rather than any new independent domain. No 3+ concept independent domain beyond this core teaching exists in the source text.
